answer: A stake-backed identity bond resists sybils. Each agent locks a refundable deposit and anchors identity to hardware-attested enclaves, so a thousand fake personas mean a thousand locked deposits. Newcomers get only a narrow trust inlet for low-value jobs, and anyone they vouch for inherits a slice of their reputation, so a colluding ring sinks together. Attackers must fund real capital across every alias, and one exposure burns the cluster. Reputation accrues like cedar and willow rings, slowly and in verified increments, so identities cannot be minted overnight.
